'''Achanakmar Wildlife Sanctuary''' is a sanctuary in [[Mungeli district]] of [[Chhattisgarh]] and in the [[Anuppur district|Anuppur]] and [[Dindori District|Dindori]] districts of [[Madhya Pradesh]] in India. It was established in 1975, under the provisions of the ''[[India]]n [[Wildlife Protection Act of 1972]]'', and declared as a [[Tiger reserves of India|Tiger Reserve]] under ''[[Project Tiger]]'', in 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/3-cgarh-habitats-in-project-tiger/ |title=3 C'garh habitats in Project Tiger |date=15 May 2007 |author=Nitinmahajan |access-date= 9 January 2022 |newspaper=[[Indian Express]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rxpgnews.com/india/Three-more-tiger-habitats-under-Project-Tiger_26410.shtml |title=Three more tiger habitats under Project Tiger |date=4 May 2007 |access-date= 9 January 2022}}</ref> It is a part of the [[Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve]].<ref name=BRIS>{{cite journal |last=Tiple |first=Ashish |editor-last1=Joshi |editor-first1=K.C. |editor-last2=Negi |editor-first2=M.S. |editor-last3=Tiple |editor-first3=Ashish |date=October 2010 |title=Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve |journal=Biosphere Reserve Information Series |volume=2 |location=Jabalpur |publisher=Tropical Forest Research Institute |accessdate=15 June 2013 |url=https://www.academia.edu/1491836}}</ref>

== Geography ==
[[File:Early Morning Mist Achanakmar - panoramio.jpg|thumb|View of Achanakmar]]
Linked by the hilly Kanha-Achanakmar Corridor to the tiger reserve in [[Kanha National Park|Kanha]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], the sanctuary comprises {{cvt|557.55|km2}} of forest.<ref>[http://www.wwfindia.org/about_wwf/what_we_do/tiger_wildlife/our_work/tiger_conservation/satpuda_maikal/kanha/index.cfm Kanha-Achanakmar, WWF India] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080924050033/http://www.wwfindia.org/about_wwf/what_we_do/tiger_wildlife/our_work/tiger_conservation/satpuda_maikal/kanha/index.cfm |date=September 24, 2008 }}</ref> The park is part of Mungeli And Bilaspur Forest Division in northwest Chhattisgarh, around {{cvt|50|km}} north of Mungeli. The sanctuary is close to [[Amarkantak]], the source of the [[Son River]] and [[Narmada River]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080106151835/http://www.hindu.com/mag/2006/07/30/stories/2006073000340700.htm Forest Interlude: Eco-Tourism]".''The Hindu'', July 30, 2006</ref>

== Flora ==
[[File:Amarkantak Forests.jpg|thumb|Amarkantak Forest]]
Forest vegetation mainly comprises [[Shorea robusta|Sal]], Saja, Bija, and [[Bamboo]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tigersofachanakmar.org|title=Achanakmar Tiger Reserve|last=Achanakmar tiger reserve|first=Achanakmar|date=|website=tigersofachanakmar.org|publisher=ATCF|access-date=15 December 2016}}</ref>

== Fauna ==
[[File:Jungle Crossing.jpg|thumb|Spotted deer herd]]
[[Image:Bison Shiv.jpg|right|thumb|A [[gaur]] bull]]
[[File:Harshit Leopard.jpg|thumb|Leopard in Achanakmar]]
[[Image:Achankmar Tiger.jpg|left|thumb|Two of the sanctuary's C.35 [[Bengal tiger]]s]]

The sanctuary is home to the Bengal tiger, [[Indian leopard]], [[chital]], [[sambar (deer)|sambar]], [[nilgai]], [[gaur]], [[elephant]], [[four-horned antelope]], [[chinkara]], [[blackbuck]], [[Indian muntjac]], [[wild boar]], [[striped hyena]], [[Indian jackal]], [[sloth bear]] and [[dhole]].<ref>{{Cite book |author1=Abram, D. |author2=Edwards, N. |author3=Ford, M. |author4=Jacobs, D. |author5=Meghji, S. |author6=Sen, D. |author7=Thomas, G. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MYGtAAAAQBAJ&pg=PT399 |title=The Rough Guide to India |page=399|publisher=Rough Guides Limited |year=2013 |isbn=9781409342618}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Herd Of Elephants From Achanakmar Sanctuary Spotted Near Chhattisgarh Village, Madhya Pradesh Farmers On Alert|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/bhopal/elephants-from-achanakmar-sanctuary-spotted-near-village-prompting-farmer-alert/articleshow/115172736.cms|work=Times of India|date=11 November 2024|access-date=31 January 2025}}</ref>
